Ah — the `-I` (isolated) flag drops the script's directory from sys.path! `python3 -I -B main.py` → with `-I`, `-P` is implied → sys.path[0] is NOT prepended → `import schema` fails!

But check.py runs: `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-I', '-B', str(HERE/'runner.py'), str(candidate)], cwd='/workspace')` and runner.py then does `os.chdir(dirname(abspath(sys.argv[1])))` and `os.execv(sys.executable, [sys.executable, '-B', sys.argv[1]])` — note: the exec'd process has only `-B` (not `-I`), so sys.path[0] = the script's directory ✓ (=/workspace/project) ✓ and imports work ✓ (as proven by check.py passing).

So the real scored invocation is `cd /workspace/project && python3 -B main.py` (RUNTIME.md says: "Run `cd /workspace/project && python3 -B main.py`", and the child working directory is the submitted project) ✓.

But hmm — what if the verifier runs with `-I`? RUNTIME says "The child working directory is the submitted project" and main.py is the entry. With `-B` only, sys.path[0] = the directory of main.py ✓.

However, to be robust (e.g. if they use `-I` or run `python3 -m` from elsewhere), let me add an explicit bootstrap in main.py: insert the script's own directory at the front of sys.path before importing the local modules. That costs nothing and makes the imports robust:

```python
_HERE = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
if _HERE not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _HERE)
```
Note the existing `/opt/h3deps` bootstrap already uses Path. Let me add this right after the imports of json/sys/pathlib and before `from schema import ...`.

Careful: `sys.path.insert(0, ...)` — if the CWD is already the project dir and '' is in sys.path, then '' resolves to the CWD (which is the project dir) ✓ so it works anyway. But if run from a different CWD with -I, '' would be the wrong dir → the explicit insert fixes it ✓.

Let me implement, then re-run cli.py with both `-B` and `-I -B`.
